questions.q: The median nerve is also known as:
questions.exp: AKA labourer's nerve. (Book p112)

questions.q: The median nerve is which type of nerve?
questions.exp: Median nerve is a mixed nerve. (Book p112)

questions.q: Motor supply of median nerve includes:
opts: Forearm anterior compartment muscles and thenar muscles
questions.exp: Motor: forearm anterior compartment muscles; hand thenar muscles. (Book p112)

questions.q: Sensory supply of median nerve on the dorsum of hand is limited to:
opts: Only the tips of lateral 3½ fingers
questions.exp: Lateral 3½ palmar; only tips dorsal. (Book p112)

questions.q: At the flexor retinaculum, the deep branch of median nerve supplies:
opts: Motor to thenar muscles and sensory to lateral 3½ finger tips
questions.exp: Deep branch: motor thenar muscles; sensory lateral 3½ finger tips. (Book p112)

questions.q: The superficial branch of median nerve at the flexor retinaculum gives:
questions.exp: Superficial branch: sensory supply palmar area. (Book p112)

questions.q: In carpal tunnel syndrome, compression of the deep branch causes:
opts: Motor atrophy of thenar eminence and paresthesia of lateral 3½ finger tips
questions.exp: Deep branch compressed → motor atrophy of thenar eminence; paresthesia, tingling and numbness of lateral 3½ finger tips. (Book p112)

questions.q: In carpal tunnel syndrome, palmar sensations remain intact because:
questions.exp: Superficial branch spared → palmar sensations intact. (Book p112)

questions.q: An autonomous zone is:
opts: An independent zone supplied by a single nerve
The area of overlap of two nerves
The root value of a nerve
questions.exp: Independent zone supplied by a single nerve. (Book p113)

questions.q: Autonomous zone of median nerve is:
questions.exp: Median nerve: tip of index finger. (Book p113)

questions.q: Autonomous zone of ulnar nerve is:
questions.exp: Ulnar nerve: tip of little finger. (Book p113)

questions.q: Autonomous zone of radial nerve is:
questions.exp: Radial nerve: dorsum of first web space. (Book p113)

questions.q: Which forearm muscle is NOT supplied by the median nerve?
questions.exp: FCU (with medial half of FDP) is supplied by ulnar nerve. (Book p113)

questions.q: The LOAF muscles of hand supplied by median nerve are:
opts: Lumbricals 1,2; opponens pollicis; abductor pollicis brevis; flexor pollicis brevis
questions.exp: LOAF: lumbricals 1,2, opponens pollicis, abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis. (Book p113)

questions.q: Which part of FDP does the median nerve supply?
questions.exp: Lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus. (Book p113)

questions.q: Median nerve supply to the arm is:
questions.exp: Arm: no supply. (Book p113)

questions.q: In the forearm, median nerve supplies:
opts: All anterior (flexor) compartment muscles except flexor carpi ulnaris and medial half of FDP
questions.exp: All anterior compartment except FCU and medial half of FDP (ulnar nerve). (Book p113)

questions.q: In the hand, median nerve supplies:
opts: All thenar muscles except adductor pollicis, plus lumbricals 1,2
questions.exp: All thenar muscles except adductor pollicis (ulnar nerve) + lumbricals 1,2. (Book p113)

questions.q: Median nerve injury at wrist is classically caused by ___ and at elbow by ___:
opts: Carpal tunnel syndrome; supracondylar humerus fracture
questions.exp: At wrist: carpal tunnel syndrome; at elbow: supracondylar humerus fracture. (Book p113)

questions.q: Order of nerve injury in supracondylar humerus fracture is:
questions.exp: Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median) > median nerve > radial nerve > ulnar nerve. (Book p113)

questions.q: Median nerve injury at wrist produces which deformity?
questions.exp: Loss of sensation lateral 3½, thenar wasting, loss of thumb abduction/flexion/opposition → ape hand/thumb deformity. (Book p113)

questions.q: In median nerve injury at wrist, thumb loses which movements?
questions.exp: Loss of thumb abduction, flexion, opposition. (Book p113)

questions.q: Treatment splint for median nerve injury at wrist is:
questions.exp: Treatment: opponens splint. (Book p114)

questions.q: Median nerve injury at elbow adds loss of functions of:
opts: FPL, FDS and FDP on top of wrist lesion manifestations
questions.exp: Manifestations of wrist lesion + loss of functions of FPL, FDS, FDP. (Book p114)

questions.q: Pen test evaluates the function of:
questions.exp: Pen test evaluates abductor pollicis brevis (abduction of thumb). (Book p114)

questions.q: Pen test procedure is:
opts: Hand palm-up on table; patient touches tip of pen hovering above palm with thumb tip; unable = positive
questions.exp: Palm facing up, touch tip of pen hovering above palm with thumb tip; unable to touch = positive pen test. (Book p114)

questions.q: Pointing index / Benediction sign / Pope sign / Oschner clasp sign evaluates:
opts: FDS (flexion of PIP & MCP) and FDP (flexion of DIP, PIP, MCP)
questions.exp: Evaluates FDS: flexion of PIP & MCP joints; FDP: flexion of DIP, PIP, MCP joints. (Book p114)

questions.q: On making a fist in median nerve injury, which finger doesn't flex?
questions.exp: Index finger doesn't flex on making a fist. (Book p114)

questions.q: As per the note, thumb abduction is movement ___ and extension ___ to the plane of palm:
questions.exp: Abduction: perpendicular to plane of palm; extension: parallel to plane of palm. (Book p114)

questions.q: Anterior interosseous nerve is:
opts: A purely motor branch of median nerve supplying FPL and lateral half of FDP
questions.exp: Branch of median nerve; purely motor; supplies FPL and lateral half of FDP. (Book p114)

questions.q: Comparing AIN palsy with median nerve palsy:
opts: AIN palsy has NO sensory deficits and NO difficulty making fist; median palsy has both
questions.exp: Table: sensory deficits − in AIN, + in median; difficulty making fist − in AIN, + in median. (Book p114)

questions.q: Miloh-Nevin sign in AIN assessment is:
questions.exp: Miloh-Nevin sign: weak OK sign. (Book p115)

questions.q: Which injury causes compression of median nerve as per the note?
questions.exp: Lunate dislocation causes compression injury of median nerve. (Book p115)

questions.q: As per summary: pen test is for ___ and pointing index for ___:
questions.exp: Pen test: for abductor pollicis brevis; pointing index: for FDP & FDS. (Book p115)

questions.q: Ulnar nerve is AKA ___ with root value ___:
questions.exp: AKA musician's nerve; root value C8, T1. (Book p115)

questions.q: Ulnar nerve motor supply in forearm is:
opts: Medial half of FDP and flexor carpi ulnaris
Lateral half of FDP and FCR
questions.exp: Forearm: medial half of FDP; flexor carpi ulnaris. (Book p115)

questions.q: Which thenar muscle is supplied by ulnar nerve?
questions.exp: Adductor pollicis (thenar muscle) → thumb adduction. (Book p115)

questions.q: Palmar interossei ___ fingers and dorsal interossei ___ fingers:
questions.exp: Palmar → adduction (PAD); dorsal → abduction (DAB). (Book p115)

questions.q: Ulnar nerve supplies which lumbricals?
questions.exp: Lumbricals 3,4. (Book p115)

questions.q: Sensory supply of ulnar nerve covers:
questions.exp: Medial 1½ fingers anteriorly & posteriorly. (Book p115)

questions.q: Sites of ulnar nerve injury are:
opts: Cubital tunnel (behind medial epicondyle) and Guyon's canal (under piso-hamate ligament)
questions.exp: 1 cubital tunnel (behind medial epicondyle); 2 Guyon's canal (under piso-hamate ligament). (Book p115)

questions.q: Ulnar nerve injury at wrist (Guyon's canal) manifests as:
opts: Partial clawing of hand, hypothenar wasting, loss of sensations in medial 1½ hand
questions.exp: Partial clawing of hand; hypothenar wasting; loss of sensations in medial 1½ hand. (Book p115)

questions.q: Complete clawing of hand results from:
questions.exp: Note: complete clawing = median + ulnar nerve palsy. (Book p115)

questions.q: Treatment splint for ulnar nerve injury is:
questions.exp: Treatment: knuckle bender splint. (Book p116)

questions.q: Card test evaluates:
questions.exp: Card test: palmar interossei (adduction of fingers). (Book p116)

questions.q: A positive card test is when:
opts: Card inserted between two extended fingers slips out easily due to weak interossei
Patient cannot grip the card with thumb
questions.exp: Examiner pulls card; weak interossei → card slips out easily (positive card test). (Book p116)

questions.q: Egawa test evaluates:
opts: Dorsal interossei (abduction of 2nd-5th fingers) by moving middle finger away from midline
questions.exp: Egawa test: dorsal interossei (abduction of 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th fingers); method: moving middle finger away from midline. (Book p116)

questions.q: Fanning fingers against resistance evaluates:
questions.exp: Fanning fingers against resistance: to evaluate dorsal interossei. (Book p116)

questions.q: Book test evaluates:
questions.exp: Book test: adductor pollicis. (Book p116)

questions.q: In book test, lack of adduction is compensated by flexors (AIN supply +), producing thumb flexion known as:
questions.exp: Lack of adduction compensated by flexors → flexion of thumb (Froment sign). (Book p116)

questions.q: Ulnar nerve injury at elbow occurs at:
questions.exp: Site of injury: in cubital tunnel, behind medial condyle. (Book p116)

questions.q: In ulnar injury at elbow, loss of medial half of FDP causes:
opts: Loss of flexion at DIP, PIP and MCP joints with LESS significant clawing
questions.exp: Loss of flexion at DIP, PIP and MCP joints → less significant clawing. (Book p116)

questions.q: Ulnar paradox states:
opts: Higher the injury of ulnar nerve, lesser the clawing/deformity
Higher the injury, more the clawing
Clawing is same at all levels
questions.exp: Ulnar paradox: higher the injury → lesser the clawing/deformity. (Book p117)

questions.q: As per ulnar assessment summary, palmar interossei are tested by ___ and adductor pollicis by ___:
questions.exp: Palmar: card test; dorsal: Egawa test/fanning; adductor pollicis: book test. (Book p117)

questions.q: Radial nerve is:
opts: m/c injured nerve but best prognosis (purely motor nerve)
questions.exp: m/c injured nerve but best prognosis (purely motor nerve). (Book p117)

questions.q: Function of radial nerve is:
opts: Extension of elbow, wrist and fingers
questions.exp: Extension of elbow, wrist & fingers. (Book p117)

questions.q: Radial nerve originates from:
questions.exp: Origin: posterior cord of brachial plexus. (Book p117)

questions.q: The first elbow extensor is:
opts: Branch of long head of triceps
Branch to medial head of triceps
questions.exp: First elbow extensor: branch of long head of triceps. (Book p117)

questions.q: The first wrist extensor is:
questions.exp: ECRL (first wrist extensor). (Book p117)

questions.q: Branches of posterior interosseous nerve (PIN) include:
opts: Branch to supinator, ECRB and extensors of fingers & thumb
questions.exp: Branches of PIN: supinator, extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensors of fingers & thumb. (Book p117)

questions.q: The superficial branch of radial nerve is a sensory branch; its autonomous zone is:
questions.exp: Superficial branch is the sensory branch (fingers excluding tips); autonomous zone: dorsum of first web space. (Book p117)

questions.q: PIN palsy (injury at radial head) manifests as:
opts: Finger drop and thumb drop without sensory loss
questions.exp: PIN palsy at radial head: finger drop, thumb drop (no sensory loss). (Book p117)

questions.q: Low radial nerve palsy occurs at ___ with manifestations ___:
opts: Lateral condyle; finger drop, thumb drop, sensory loss
questions.exp: Low radial nerve palsy at lateral condyle: finger drop, thumb drop, sensory loss. (Book p117)

questions.q: High radial nerve palsy (m/c) occurs at ___ adding ___:
questions.exp: High radial nerve palsy (m/c) at spiral groove: finger drop, thumb drop, sensory loss, wrist drop. (Book p117)

questions.q: Very high radial nerve palsy occurs at ___ with the extra feature ___:
questions.exp: Very high palsy at axilla: adds inability to extend elbow. (Book p117)

questions.q: Injury proximal to ECRL (spiral groove) gives wrist drop ___; distal to ECRL gives wrist drop ___:
questions.exp: Proximal to ECRL (spiral groove): wrist drop +; distal to ECRL: wrist drop −. (Book p117)

questions.q: Holstein-Lewis fracture is:
opts: m/c cause of radial nerve injury — humeral shaft fracture between upper 1/3 and lower 1/3 entrapping the nerve
questions.exp: m/c cause of radial nerve injury: fracture of shaft of humerus between upper 1/3 and lower 1/3 causing radial nerve entrapment. (Book p118)

questions.q: Holstein-Lewis fracture produces:
opts: Wrist drop, finger drop, thumb drop, sensory loss
questions.exp: Causes radial nerve entrapment → wrist drop, finger drop, thumb drop, sensory loss. (Book p118)

questions.q: Cock-up splint is Rx for:
questions.exp: Cock up splint (Rx for wrist drop). (Book p118)

questions.q: Static cock-up splint ___ while dynamic cock-up splint ___:
opts: Extends wrist; extends wrist + allows flexion of fingers
Allows finger flexion; extends wrist only
questions.exp: Static: extends wrist; dynamic: extends wrist + allows flexion of fingers. (Book p118)

questions.q: As per the nerve test summary, Froment sign means:
opts: Flexor pollicis substitutes for adductor pollicis
questions.exp: Froment sign: flexor pollicis substitutes for adductor pollicis. (Book p118)

questions.q: Kiloh-Nevin sign / pincer grasp tests:
questions.exp: Kiloh Nevin sign/pincer grasp: flexor digitorum profundus + flexor pollicis longus (AIN). (Book p118)

questions.q: In the summary table, finger & thumb drop indicates ___ and wrist drop indicates ___:
questions.exp: Finger & thumb drop: extensors (PIN); wrist drop: extensors of wrist ECRL. (Book p118)

questions.q: Sciatic nerve injury causes manifestations of:
questions.exp: If injured causes manifestations of CPN nerve injury. (Book p119)

questions.q: On sciatic nerve cross-section:
opts: Common peroneal fibres lie peripheral, tibial fibres central
questions.exp: Cross section: CPN fibres outer, tibial nerve fibres inner. (Book p119)

questions.q: The m/c cause of sciatic nerve injury is:
questions.exp: Iatrogenic (hip surgeries): m/c cause; also posterior dislocation, gunshot, gluteal injections. (Book p119)

questions.q: Superficial branch of common peroneal nerve supplies:
opts: Motor: lateral compartment of leg (evertors of foot); sensory: dorsum of foot
Motor: anterior compartment; sensory: first web space
questions.exp: Superficial branch: motor lateral compartment (evertors); sensory dorsum of foot. (Book p119)

questions.q: Deep branch of common peroneal nerve supplies:
opts: Motor: anterior compartment (dorsiflexors of ankle, inversion of foot); sensory: 1st web space of foot
questions.exp: Deep branch: sensory 1st web space; motor anterior compartment: dorsiflexors of ankle, inversion of foot. (Book p119)

questions.q: Common peroneal nerve is classically injured by:
questions.exp: Causes of injury: fracture of neck of fibula. (Book p119)

questions.q: Common peroneal nerve injury causes loss of ankle dorsiflexion and eversion, producing:
questions.exp: Loss of dorsiflexion & eversion → equinovarus deformity (plantar flexion & inversion). (Book p119)

questions.q: Gait in foot drop is:
opts: High stepping/foot-drop gait/steppage gait to overcome dragging of foot
questions.exp: High stepping/foot-drop gait/steppage gait (to overcome dragging of foot d/t foot drop). (Book p119)

questions.q: Splint used for foot drop is:
questions.exp: Splint: foot drop splint/Ankle Foot Orthosis (AFO). (Book p120)

questions.q: Entrapment neuropathy means:
opts: Nerve trapped under a structure causing delayed conduction of stimulus
questions.exp: Nerve trapped under a structure → delayed conduction of stimulus. (Book p120)

questions.q: Carpal tunnel syndrome is entrapment of median nerve under:
questions.exp: Median nerve entrapment in carpal tunnel (at wrist) under flexor retinaculum/transverse carpal ligament. (Book p120)

questions.q: The m/c entrapment neuropathy and m/c entrapped nerve are:
questions.exp: m/c entrapment neuropathy; m/c entrapped nerve: median nerve. (Book p120)

questions.q: The m/c cause of carpal tunnel syndrome is:
questions.exp: Idiopathic: m/c cause. (Book p120)

questions.q: Which endocrine conditions cause carpal tunnel syndrome by raising tunnel pressure?
opts: Hypothyroidism (myxedema), pregnancy (fluid retention), acromegaly and diabetes mellitus
questions.exp: Hypothyroidism (myxedema), pregnancy (fluid retention), acromegaly (bone & soft tissue overgrowth), diabetes mellitus. (Book p120)

questions.q: Which fracture can cause carpal tunnel syndrome via hematoma?
questions.exp: Colles' fracture (hematoma → compression). (Book p120)

questions.q: Carpal tunnel syndrome classically affects:
questions.exp: Middle aged female. (Book p121)

questions.q: The pain of CTS is ___ in type, distributed along ___ and maximum ___:
opts: Burning pins & needles; lateral 3½ fingers; at night
Dull aching; whole arm; at morning
questions.exp: Burning pins & needle type of pain along lateral 3½ fingers, maximum at night. (Book p121)

questions.q: CTS pain is relieved by:
opts: Shaking the hand or hanging hand at the edge of bed
questions.exp: Relieved on shaking her hand; hanging hand at the edge of bed. (Book p121)

questions.q: Phalen's test and reverse Phalen's test require holding the position for:
opts: Approx 1 minute, producing dull aching pain, numbness, paraesthesia, tingling along median nerve distribution
questions.exp: Position held for approx 1 minute → dull aching pain, numbness, paraesthesia, tingling along median nerve distribution. (Book p121)

questions.q: The BEST clinical test for CTS is:
opts: Durkan's test — direct median nerve compression between thenar & hypothenar eminence for 30 seconds
questions.exp: Durkan's test: best clinical test; direct median nerve compression between thenar & hypothenar eminence for 30 seconds → reproduces symptoms. (Book p121)

questions.q: IOC for carpal tunnel syndrome is:
opts: Nerve conduction studies — decreased velocity due to compression under flexor retinaculum
questions.exp: Nerve conduction studies: IOC; determines velocity; decreased velocity d/t nerve compression under flexor retinaculum. (Book p121)

questions.q: Treatment of CTS proceeds as:
opts: Conservative (rest, steroids, splints); if no improvement, surgery releasing flexor retinaculum/transverse carpal ligament
questions.exp: Conservative: rest, steroids, splints; no improvement → surgery: release of flexor retinaculum/transverse carpal ligament. (Book p121)

questions.q: Allen's test is used to:
opts: Assess patency of vasculature of hand before performing arterial procedures (arterial line)
questions.exp: Allen's test: to assess patency of vasculature of hand before performing arterial procedures (arterial line). (Book p121)

questions.q: Opposition of thumb is performed by ___ supplied by ___:
opts: Opponens pollicis; deep branch of median nerve
questions.exp: Opponens pollicis → supplied by deep branch of median nerve. (Book p122)

questions.q: The only function completely lost in CTS is:
questions.exp: Only function completely lost in CTS: opposition of thumb. (Book p122)

questions.q: Meralgia paraesthetica is entrapment of:
opts: Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh under inguinal ligament
questions.exp: Entrapment of lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh under inguinal ligament. (Book p122)

questions.q: Meralgia paraesthetica causes ___ and is caused by ___:
opts: Burning sensation along lateral aspect of thigh; overweight and tight clothing around hip
questions.exp: Burning sensation along lateral aspect of thigh; etiology: overweight, tight clothing around hip. (Book p122)

questions.q: Cubital tunnel entrapment involves which nerve at which site?
opts: Ulnar; behind the medial condyle humerus
questions.exp: Cubital tunnel: ulnar behind the medial condyle humerus. (Book p122)

questions.q: Guyon's canal entrapment involves which nerve at which site?
questions.exp: Guyon's canal: ulnar under the piso-hamate ligament. (Book p122)

questions.q: Pronator syndrome is entrapment of:
opts: Median nerve at heads of pronator teres
questions.exp: Pronator syndrome: median nerve at heads of pronator teres. (Book p122)

questions.q: Kiloh-Nevin syndrome is entrapment of ___ at ___:
questions.exp: Kiloh Nevin syndrome: AIN at supracondylar humerus fracture. (Book p122)

questions.q: Cheiralgia paraesthetica is entrapment of:
opts: Superficial radial nerve at radial styloid/brachioradialis insertion (wrist watch, cuffs, bangles)
Deep radial nerve at spiral groove
questions.exp: Superficial radial nerve at radial styloid, insertion of brachioradialis (wrist watch, cuffs, bangles). (Book p122)

questions.q: Pyriformis syndrome entraps:
opts: Sciatic nerve between pyriformis & obturator internus muscle
questions.exp: Sciatic nerve at pyriformis & obturator internus muscle. (Book p122)

questions.q: Tarsal tunnel syndrome entraps:
opts: Posterior tibial nerve behind medial malleolus below flexor retinaculum of foot (RA)
questions.exp: Posterior tibial nerve behind medial malleolus below the flexor retinaculum of foot (RA). (Book p122)

questions.q: Morton metatarsalgia entraps:
opts: Interdigital nerve of foot between 3rd & 4th toe
questions.exp: Interdigital nerve of foot between 3rd & 4th toe. (Book p122)

units.title: Median Nerve: Labourer's Nerve
units.guide: The labourer's nerve is mixed: motor to forearm flexors and thenar muscles, sensory to lateral 3½ palm and only the tips dorsally. At the retinaculum it splits — deep branch (thenar motor + tip sensation) and superficial (palmar sensation). CTS squeezes the deep branch, sparing palmar feeling.

units.title: Autonomous Zones
units.guide: An autonomous zone is one nerve's private patch: index tip (median), little finger tip (ulnar), first web space dorsum (radial).

units.title: Median Motor Map & LOAF
units.guide: Arm: nothing. Forearm: every flexor except FCU and medial FDP (ulnar's share). Hand: the LOAF — lumbricals 1,2, opponens, abductor and flexor pollicis brevis — all thenar but adductor pollicis, which is ulnar.

units.title: Median Injuries: Wrist & Elbow
units.guide: Wrist lesions come from carpal tunnel, elbow lesions from supracondylar fractures — where AIN tops the injury order ahead of median, radial, ulnar. Wrist injury: numb lateral 3½, wasted thenar, ape thumb; add FPL/FDS/FDP loss at elbow. Opponens splint treats.

units.title: Median Tests & AIN
units.guide: Pen test lifts the thumb (APB); pointing index/benediction exposes FDS+FDP failure with the unflexed index; AIN — purely motor to FPL and lateral FDP — shows a weak OK (Miloh-Nevin) sign with no sensory loss and an easy fist. Lunate dislocation can squeeze the median.

units.title: Ulnar: Musician's Nerve
units.guide: C8-T1 musician's nerve: forearm FCU and medial FDP; hand hypothenar, adductor pollicis, interossei (palmar adduct, dorsal abduct), lumbricals 3,4; senses medial 1½ all round. Cubital tunnel and Guyon's canal trap it; wrist lesions claw partially — complete clawing needs median too.

units.title: Ulnar Tests & the Paradox
units.guide: Knuckle bender splint supports the claw. Card test = palmar interossei (card slips), Egawa and fanning = dorsal interossei, book test = adductor pollicis with Froment's thumb-flexion cheat. Elbow lesions spare clawing because FDP's medial half dies too — the ulnar paradox: higher injury, lesser claw.

units.title: Radial Nerve: Levels of Palsy
units.guide: Most injured yet best prognosis — purely motor, extending elbow, wrist, fingers from the posterior cord. Long-head triceps branch fires first; ECRL is the first wrist extensor; PIN takes supinator, ECRB and finger extensors. Levels: radial head (PIN: finger+thumb drop), lateral condyle (+sensory), spiral groove (+wrist drop, m/c), axilla (+elbow extension lost). Below ECRL, no wrist drop.

units.title: Holstein-Lewis, Splints & Test Tables
units.guide: Holstein-Lewis — humeral shaft fracture at the upper/lower third junction — entraps radial nerve, the m/c cause. Cock-up splint answers wrist drop: static extends wrist, dynamic also lets fingers flex. The summary tables pair every sign with its muscle, Froment to pincer grasp.

units.title: Sciatic & Common Peroneal
units.guide: Sciatic injury behaves like CPN injury — peroneal fibres ride peripherally around the tibial core; hip surgeries top the causes. At the fibular neck the CPN splits: superficial everts and feels the dorsum, deep dorsiflexes and feels the first web. Fibular neck fracture drops the foot into equinovarus and a steppage gait; AFO splints it.

units.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
units.guide: Trapped under the flexor retinaculum, the median — m/c entrapped nerve in the m/c entrapment neuropathy — burns at night along lateral 3½ fingers in middle-aged women, eased by shaking or hanging the hand. Idiopathic leads causes; myxedema, pregnancy, acromegaly, Colles' hematoma, gout, amyloid, diabetes follow. Durkan's 30-second compression is the best clinical test, NCS the IOC; rest-steroid-splint first, then release the ligament. Allen's test clears the hand's vessels before arterial lines.

units.title: Opposition & Meralgia
units.guide: Opponens pollicis, deep median branch, performs opposition — the single function CTS destroys completely. Meralgia paraesthetica burns the lateral thigh where the lateral cutaneous nerve ducks under the inguinal ligament, pinched by overweight and tight clothing.

units.title: The Entrapment Table
units.guide: Memorise the grid: cubital tunnel — ulnar behind medial condyle; Guyon's — ulnar under piso-hamate; pronator syndrome — median at pronator teres heads; Kiloh-Nevin — AIN in supracondylar fracture; cheiralgia — superficial radial at the styloid (watch, cuffs, bangles); meralgia — lateral femoral cutaneous under inguinal ligament; pyriformis — sciatic; tarsal tunnel — posterior tibial behind medial malleolus; Morton — interdigital nerve, 3rd-4th toe.
